skill.name: onboard
skill.description: Design or improve onboarding flows, empty states, and first-time user experiences that help users reach value quickly.
skill.summary: Design user onboarding, empty states, guided tours, and first-use education that move users toward value quickly.
skill.author: pbakaus

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline Markdown formatting, and UX guidance in SKILL.md. I found no evidence of shell execution, system reconnaissance, data exfiltration, prompt injection, or malicious intent in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - Keyboard shortcut hints (`⌘K` shown on search box)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 112 is a Markdown code fence that opens a plain text empty-state example. It does not invoke Ruby, shell execution, or any external command.
Line 116 is the closing Markdown code fence for the empty-state copy example. There is no executable shell or Ruby backtick usage.
Line 178 uses inline Markdown backticks around a help icon label. This is documentation formatting, not command execution.

content.value_statement: New users often leave when a product does not explain its value quickly. This skill helps design onboarding, empty states, and guided help that move users to first success.
actual_capabilities: Defines onboarding questions about user goals, experience level, time commitment, and success metrics.
Recommends welcome screens, account setup, core concept introductions, and first success moments.
Designs empty states with value, next action, examples, visual support, and help links.
Plans tooltips, feature announcements, guided tours, and interactive tutorials.
Lists implementation patterns for tours, modals, progress tracking, and analytics.
Suggests quality checks for completion, comprehension, skip rate, and time to value.
limitations: Does not include executable implementation files or reusable UI components.
Requires product context to produce specific onboarding copy and flows.
Does not run usability tests or collect analytics by itself.
Mentions third-party libraries but does not install or configure them.

use_cases.title: Create a First-Use Flow
use_cases.description: Plan the welcome, setup, core concept, and first success steps for a new product experience.

use_cases.title: Improve Empty States
use_cases.description: Turn blank pages into useful entry points with value copy, examples, actions, and help links.

use_cases.title: Audit Feature Adoption
use_cases.description: Review tooltips, tours, and tutorials for clarity, timing, skip paths, and repeat behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Onboarding Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new product or feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an onboarding flow for [product or feature]. The target users are [audience]. The desired aha moment is [moment].

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite an Empty State
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a blank state that users see before creating content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this empty state: [current copy or screenshot notes]. Explain the value, add a clear action, and suggest one helpful example.

prompt_templates.title: Design Contextual Help
prompt_templates.scenario: Add tooltips, hints, or announcements to a complex workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create contextual help for [workflow]. Include trigger moments, tooltip copy, dismiss behavior, and links to deeper help.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Onboarding Journey
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing onboarding experience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this onboarding journey: [steps, screens, or notes]. Identify friction, missing context, weak skip paths, and time-to-value risks.

output_examples.input: Design onboarding for a project management app where users need to create their first project.
output_examples.output: A three-step flow: welcome with value, project setup with smart defaults, and first task creation with a template option.

output_examples.input: Improve an empty reports page for a new analytics user.
output_examples.output: A revised empty state explaining what reports show, why they matter, and offering Create report or Start from template actions.

output_examples.input: Review a seven-step guided tour for a complex admin console.
output_examples.output: A shorter workflow-based tour, stronger skip path, replay option, and analytics checks for completion and drop-off.

best_practices: Start by defining the target user, desired aha moment, and minimum successful action.
Make onboarding optional when possible and preserve a clear skip path.
Track completion and dismissals so users do not see the same prompt repeatedly.
anti_patterns: Forcing every user through a long tour before they can use the product.
Explaining every feature upfront instead of teaching the next useful action.
Showing tooltips repeatedly after users dismiss or complete them.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps design onboarding flows, empty states, guided tours, tooltips, tutorials, and first-use education.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, patterns, and small illustrative snippets, but it does not implement UI components.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the product area, target users, current friction, desired aha moment, and known success metrics.

faq.question: Is this useful for existing products?
faq.answer: Yes. It can audit current onboarding, empty states, feature announcements, and help patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace user research?
faq.answer: No. It suggests usability checks and metrics, but real user testing remains necessary.
